subject: Agriculture
title: Composting at Scale
description: A micro-lesson that makes Composting at Scale usable.

hook.text: San Francisco diverts food waste from landfills and turns it into compost for wine country farms. A perfect loop.

buildup.text: Composting converts organic waste into stable humus—rich in nutrients and beneficial microorganisms.

discovery.text: Adding compost to soil increases water-holding capacity by up to 20%—critical in drought-prone regions.

twist.text: Poorly managed compost piles go anaerobic and emit methane—worse than landfill if done wrong.

climax.text: Large-scale composting requires careful temperature management—55–65°C to kill pathogens and weed seeds.

punchline.text: Rot done right is gold for soil. Rot done wrong is just more pollution.

quiz.question: What temperature range must large-scale compost reach to kill pathogens?
